name: NE Couloir

pitch_detail.notes: Moderate, continuous snow climbing from the cirque into the gully.
Steepens noticeably; one of the route's steeper sections.
Narrows further and may require scrambling over rock depending on snow coverage; limited protection/anchor options — the reported crux of the route.

rappels: None documented — walk-off descent; note the first-ascent party specifically reported that an emergency/rope descent from the crux would be difficult due to limited anchor placements.
descent_text: From the top of the couloir on the summit ridge, walk off via Tiffany's northwest ridge, then drop to the old unmaintained trail above Little Tiffany Lake, following it down to rejoin trail #373 near Honeymoon Pass and retracing the approach back to Tiffany Springs Campground. Allow roughly 5 hours round-trip from the trailhead.
approach: From Tiffany Springs Campground (6,760 ft), hike trail #373 east past Tiffany Lake to Honeymoon Pass (7,150 ft, ~45 min). From the pass, traverse SW/south along the east slope below the ridge crest to the small cirque at the base of the North Face (7,360 ft), then continue to the base of the couloir. Driving access: via Conconully/North Fork Salmon Creek (~21 mi, ~1 hr, rough road, 4WD recommended), via the South Fork/Baldy Pass (~30.6 mi, ~2 hr, 2WD gravel), or via the Methow Valley (~26.5 mi, ~1 hr, 2WD gravel).
overview: The longest and most continuous narrow snow gully on the left side of Tiffany's north face, averaging 40 degrees with steeper sections to 55 degrees.
beta: A sustained snow climb with a crux at the upper narrow section. Approximately 5-hour round trip from trailhead depending on conditions. Route requires good snow conditions and avalanche awareness.
